In contrast, `desktop/modal.scss` sets `.custom-message-length` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, matching the previous intent/pattern (lighter in light theme, darker in dark theme). This inconsistency is directly verifiable in the diff and likely an accidental inversion of the lightness values for mobile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Lightness-pair maintenance burden: every site must hand-compute the complementary secondary lightness (100%−N%), inviting silent-flip drift; the fix should also audit the whole diff for the pattern where the light argument was changed from its original value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces many single `scale-color($primary, $lightness: N%)` values with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: N%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: M%))`, where `M` is usually manually set to the complementary `100%-N` (e.g., 40/60, 70/30, 75/25, 25/75). That does create an ongoing maintenance burden and risk of drift because the complement is hand-computed throughout many files. Additionally, the diff does include cases where the primary lightness argument changed from the original value (suggesting the audit requested by the finding is actionable), e.g. in `desktop/topic-post.scss` an `a` color changes from `$lightness: 30%` to a `dark-light-choose` using `$lightness: 70%`, and in `mobile/modal.scss` `.custom-message-length` changes from `$lightness: 70%` to `$lightness: 30%` on the primary side. These are concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/scope concerns, but not a provable functional defect from the diff alone.
